front: Core idea of Drill 01: Arrays?
back: Traverse arrays with clear index control.

front: When does “Drill 01: Arrays” appear?
back: In-place mutation, basic scanning, prefix accumulation.

front: In Drill 01: Arrays: what is “Two-pointer swap”?
back: Use left and right for in-place reverse.

front: In Drill 01: Arrays: what is “Single pass selection”?
back: Track best index/value while scanning.

front: In Drill 01: Arrays: what is “Accumulation”?
back: Maintain running total for sums and prefix output.

front: In Drill 01: Arrays: what is “Rotation logic”?
back: Reduce k with modulo and transform indices safely.

front: Core idea of Drill 02: Hashing?
back: Trade memory for fast lookup.

front: When does “Drill 02: Hashing” appear?
back: Need membership checks, counting, grouping by signature.

front: In Drill 02: Hashing: what is “Complement lookup”?
back: For target pair questions, check map before inserting.

front: In Drill 02: Hashing: what is “Seen set”?
back: Detect duplicates in O(1) average lookup per element.

front: In Drill 02: Hashing: what is “Frequency table”?
back: Count occurrences with map[key]++.

front: In Drill 02: Hashing: what is “Canonical key”?
back: Group equivalent strings (anagrams) by a normalized form.

front: Core idea of Drill 03: Two Pointers and Sliding Window?
back: Keep constraints with pointer movement instead of nested loops.
section: Drill 03: Two Pointers and Sliding Window

front: When does “Drill 03: Two Pointers and Sliding Window” appear?
back: Sorted arrays, in-place filtering, contiguous window metrics.
section: Drill 03: Two Pointers and Sliding Window

front: In Drill 03: Two Pointers and Sliding Window: what is “Read/write pointers”?
back: Compact valid values to the front in one pass.
section: Drill 03: Two Pointers and Sliding Window

front: In Drill 03: Two Pointers and Sliding Window: what is “Opposite-end pointers”?
back: Move boundaries based on rule (area/palindrome logic).
section: Drill 03: Two Pointers and Sliding Window

front: In Drill 03: Two Pointers and Sliding Window: what is “Fixed window”?
back: Build first window, then slide by add-right/remove-left.
section: Drill 03: Two Pointers and Sliding Window

front: In Drill 03: Two Pointers and Sliding Window: what is “Invariant thinking”?
back: Each pointer move must preserve correctness condition.
section: Drill 03: Two Pointers and Sliding Window

front: Core idea of Drill 04: Binary Search?
back: Use sorted structure to discard half each step.

front: When does “Drill 04: Binary Search” appear?
back: Exact search, insertion point, rotated sorted arrays.

front: In Drill 04: Binary Search: what is “Search space boundaries”?
back: lo, hi, and loop condition define correctness.

front: In Drill 04: Binary Search: what is “Midpoint safety”?
back: mid := lo + (hi-lo)/2.

front: In Drill 04: Binary Search: what is “Lower bound”?
back: Find first index where condition becomes true.

front: In Drill 04: Binary Search: what is “Half-sorted decision”?
back: In rotated arrays, detect which half is ordered.

front: Core idea of Drill 05: Trees and Stacks?
back: Use stack discipline for nested structure and next-greater relations.

front: When does “Drill 05: Trees and Stacks” appear?
back: Tree traversal, bracket matching, nearest next condition.

front: In Drill 05: Trees and Stacks: what is “Traversal state”?
back: Recursion or explicit stack to simulate call stack.

front: In Drill 05: Trees and Stacks: what is “Depth recurrence”?
back: Tree answers often combine left and right subtree results.

front: In Drill 05: Trees and Stacks: what is “LIFO matching”?
back: Parentheses validation uses most recent unmatched opener.

front: In Drill 05: Trees and Stacks: what is “Monotonic stack”?
back: Maintain decreasing/increasing stack for next-greater problems.

front: Core idea of Drill 06: Dynamic Programming (1D)?
back: Build answers from solved smaller subproblems.

front: When does “Drill 06: Dynamic Programming (1D)” appear?
back: "Min cost", "max value", "count ways" on linear states.

front: In Drill 06: Dynamic Programming (1D): what is “State definition first”?
back: Write what dp[i] means before coding.

front: In Drill 06: Dynamic Programming (1D): what is “Base cases”?
back: Initialize smallest known states correctly.

front: In Drill 06: Dynamic Programming (1D): what is “Transition rule”?
back: Express current answer from prior states.

front: In Drill 06: Dynamic Programming (1D): what is “Take/skip pattern”?
back: For adjacency constraints, compare include vs exclude.

front: Core idea of Drill 07: Graphs (Grid BFS/DFS)?
back: Explore connected cells with traversal rules.

front: When does “Drill 07: Graphs (Grid BFS/DFS)” appear?
back: Components in grids, fill regions, shortest unweighted path.

front: In Drill 07: Graphs (Grid BFS/DFS): what is “DFS/BFS component scan”?
back: Start traversal from each unvisited valid cell.

front: In Drill 07: Graphs (Grid BFS/DFS): what is “Visited control”?
back: Prevent revisits and infinite loops.

front: In Drill 07: Graphs (Grid BFS/DFS): what is “Neighbor generation”?
back: Standard 4-direction moves with boundary checks.

front: In Drill 07: Graphs (Grid BFS/DFS): what is “BFS distance layers”?
back: First time reaching a node gives shortest path in unweighted graphs.

front: Core idea of Drill 10: Math?
back: Number-theory helpers that appear inside many DSA solutions.

front: When does “Drill 10: Math” appear?
back: Modular counting, cycle alignment, combinatorics, prime checks, bit sizing.

front: In Drill 10: Math: what is “Euclidean GCD”?
back: gcd(a,b) = gcd(b, a mod b) until b == 0.

front: In Drill 10: Math: what is “LCM from GCD”?
back: lcm(a,b) = |a*b| / gcd(a,b).

front: In Drill 10: Math: what is “Modular exponentiation”?
back: Square-and-multiply in O(log exp).

front: In Drill 10: Math: what is “Combinations”?
back: Use k = min(k, n-k) and multiplicative formula to avoid overflow.

front: In Drill 10: Math: what is “Prime test”?
back: Check 2, then odd divisors up to √n.

front: In Drill 10: Math: what is “Power of two”?

front: Pattern picker: Count/group occurrences → ?
back: Frequency map

front: Pattern picker: Next greater element → ?
back: Monotonic stack

front: Pattern picker: Min/max ways over sequence → ?
back: 1D DP

front: Pattern picker: Grid region count/fill → ?
back: DFS/BFS

front: Pattern picker: Shortest path in unweighted grid → ?
back: BFS

front: Pattern picker: GCD / LCM / mod exponent → ?
back: Number theory (Drill 10)

front: Pattern picker: Count combinations mod m → ?
back: nCr + modPow
